explanation: The ways to reach a stair are the sum of ways to reach its preceding maximum_step stairs. Maintain that sliding sum as each new stair enters and the oldest eligible stair leaves. There is one empty sequence at stair zero; without any allowed positive step, no higher stair is reachable.
timeComplexity: O(top). The sliding window changes in O(1) per height; recursive versions explicitly sum up to maximum_step predecessor states.
spaceComplexity: O(top). Counts are stored for heights 0 through top; recursive variants also retain at most top frames.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Partition climbs by their final step size. A climb ending at stair t comes uniquely from one of the preceding maximum_step stairs, so their counts sum without overlap. The rolling window maintains exactly those eligible counts; ways[0]=1 represents the empty climb.
walkthrough: For top 5 and maximum step 2, the counts at stairs 0 through 5 are 1,1,2,3,5,8. Each new count adds the two previous ones, giving 8 ordered climbs. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: There is one way to stay at stair zero.
When only step size 1 is allowed, every reachable top has one climb.
